title: The best lists to keep — and the best ways to keep them
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: Version History
recommendations.blurb: I’m sorry, I’m sorry, more self-promotion. (I’m not sorry.) Our new show is launching this weekend! You can watch on The Verge ’s YouTube channel, or on The Vergecast ’s feed, but my big request is that you subscribe wherever you get podcasts. And give us five stars. And tell your friends.

recommendations.name: Sora
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been using this “TikTok but it’s all AI videos” app for a couple of days, and I still don’t know if it’s a brilliant idea or a totally horrifying one. But I’ll tell you this: the quality of stuff Sora 2 can produce is pretty astonishing.

recommendations.name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
recommendations.blurb: All the developer types I know are thrilled about how good Claude Code is becoming, and 4.5 gives the model the power and patience to do much more complicated stuff. I think I’m going to finally finish vibe coding my perfect note-taking app with this one.

recommendations.name: Ghost of Yōtei
recommendations.blurb: A sequel to the massively successful Ghost of Tsushima, this PS5 game is a completely different story but appears to be just as intense, just as sprawling, and just as compelling. Oh, and everybody keeps raving about how fun the fighting is.

recommendations.name: Comet
recommendations.blurb: Perplexity’s AI-forward browser is finally out and available to everyone. I’ve used it a little, and my main impression is that it’s a lot like every other AI-forward browser?

recommendations.name: Amazon’s Kindle Scribe Colorsoft
recommendations.blurb: Amazon prioritized all the right things with the new Scribe, from lower-latency writing to integrating with other productivity tools. The Colorsoft is $630, which is way too much for an e-reader, but I know a lot of note-takers and comic book fans who are excited about it anyway.

recommendations.name: Amazon’s Echo Dot Max
recommendations.blurb: Honestly, all of Amazon’s new stuff looks great — though I’m not recommending any of the fancier stuff until Alexa Plus proves itself. But if you’re like, blah blah AI who cares whatever just play me some music and set some timers, this little speaker sounds like a winner.

recommendations.name: Final Fantasy Tactics: The Ivalice Chronicles
recommendations.blurb: I know almost nothing about Final Fantasy, and frankly I’m terrified to learn because all my FF -fan friends and colleagues are super into the new title and it seems like the exact right amount of complexity to hook me forever. Please, nobody else tell me how fun this game is.

recommendations.name: Kagi News
recommendations.blurb: Kagi continues to be my daily-driver search engine, and this is a good new addition to the product: a once-daily digest of big news stories, with AI summaries but mostly lots of broadly sourced reading material. Simple, straightforward, super useful.

recommendations.name: Adobe Premiere for iOS
recommendations.blurb: We knew this was coming, but now it’s here: the mobile version of Adobe’s popular video editing app. I definitely wouldn’t expect pro-level quality, and not every feature is here, but the app seems like a strong start. And Android is supposedly coming soon!

recommendations.name: Logitech’s MX Master 4
recommendations.blurb: Everybody you know who cares about their computer mouse probably has an MX Master. And with good reason!

recommendations.name: The birth of the Excel spreadsheet
recommendations.blurb: “ The birth of the Excel spreadsheet.” Microsoft’s ubiquitous spreadsheet app turned 40 this week, and the BBC has a really fun nine-minute podcast history lesson about why rows and columns took over the world.

recommendations.name: A bunch of you keep packing lists, sometimes several of them for different kinds
recommendations.blurb: A bunch of you keep packing lists, sometimes several of them for different kinds of trips. I’ve never done it, but I love the idea of a lower-stress system for making sure you bring the right stuff.

recommendations.name: Otto said they keep a list of saved product manuals and documents, in PDF form
recommendations.blurb: Otto said they keep a list of saved product manuals and documents, in PDF form, for easy retrieval.

recommendations.name: Ron has a list of people they want to keep in touch with, and tries to get to a
recommendations.blurb: Ron has a list of people they want to keep in touch with, and tries to get to a few of them a week. (Ron also keeps a list of paint color names they use, which would have saved me a lot of time the last two weeks.)

recommendations.name: Lee keeps a list of pictures their kids created in restaurants, and of all the k
recommendations.blurb: Lee keeps a list of pictures their kids created in restaurants, and of all the kid-related gifts they’ve received.

recommendations.name: Hannes has a list of their favorite quotes from books, and another one that’s a
recommendations.blurb: Hannes has a list of their favorite quotes from books, and another one that’s a list of “personal best nostalgia-bait” songs from their youth.

recommendations.name: Pen and paper
recommendations.blurb: A surprising winner here! I heard from so many of you that you’ve tried the apps, you’ve moved between platforms, and you went back to good ol’ writing stuff down. This may just be the way.

recommendations.name: Todoist
recommendations.blurb: I heard about a lot of to-do list apps, but Todoist seems to be the consensus favorite. It’s flexible, it’s fast, it’s available everywhere, I get it.

recommendations.name: Notion
recommendations.blurb: The other app that came up over and over, especially for people who keep really complex systems — not just a list of movies to watch, but a list of starred reviews for every movie you’ve ever seen. Notion’s great at that.

recommendations.name: Google Keep
recommendations.blurb: The built-in apps. Lots of shouts for Google Keep from the Android crowd, and many fans of Apple Notes and Apple Reminders among the iOS users.

recommendations.name: Google Sheets
recommendations.blurb: Spreadsheets. I heard about Google Sheets, and Excel, and Smartsheet. Turns out a lot of you are big fans of spreadsheeting just about anything. To which I say: I love it, but the mobile apps are all so terrible!

recommendations.name: Craft
recommendations.blurb: Honorable Mentions: Craft and Obsidian both got some love in the note-taking world. AnyList is a favorite for grocery shoppers in particular. Letterboxd and Trakt seem to be the best for tracking shows and movies.

recommendations.name: Pixel 10 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro
recommendations.blurb: The phones: Pixel 10 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro.

recommendations.name: Backdrops
recommendations.blurb: The wallpaper: Both from the Backdrops app.

recommendations.name: Not Boring Weather
recommendations.blurb: The iPhone uses the Not Boring Weather app widget, but I use Carrot Weather to actually dig into details.

recommendations.name: Carrot Weather
recommendations.blurb: The iPhone uses the Not Boring Weather app widget, but I use Carrot Weather to actually dig into details.

recommendations.name: Connections
recommendations.blurb: I’m really into the Sports-themed Connections game by The New York Times right now.

recommendations.name: Athlytic
recommendations.blurb: Also very much into this app called Athlytic that takes all my Apple Watch / health data and displays it in a very Whoop-like way, without me needing to also wear a Whoop.

recommendations.name: Arc
recommendations.blurb: Also very unfortunately still loving using Arc on desktop and mobile, and am in desperate need of a new browser since Arc is betraying us all.

recommendations.name: FIIO RR11
recommendations.blurb: My partner and I got really into the drive-in movie scene in the Hudson Valley, but sitting in our pickup bed instead of the front seats. The problem became how to get great audio over a portable radio. Currently testing: FIIO RR11 portable radio for FM signal, then aux into a Soundcore Motion x600.

recommendations.name: Soundcore Motion x600
recommendations.blurb: My partner and I got really into the drive-in movie scene in the Hudson Valley, but sitting in our pickup bed instead of the front seats. The problem became how to get great audio over a portable radio. Currently testing: FIIO RR11 portable radio for FM signal, then aux into a Soundcore Motion x600.

recommendations.name: Super Mario Galaxy 2
recommendations.blurb: Paying too much for it, but revisiting Super Mario Galaxy 2 in 4K on the Switch 2 is so wonderful!

recommendations.name: Everlog
recommendations.blurb: I would like to recommend Everlog for your diary / journal. You can get a lifetime subscription and, one of my favorite features, add updates to previous entries.

recommendations.name: Digimon Story: Time Stranger
recommendations.blurb: Getting ready for Digimon Story: Time Stranger. Gonna play on the PS5. Demo was fun, and it’s turning out to be the best Digimon game ever reviewed. With the new anime also starting next week, us Digimon fans are eating well.

recommendations.name: The Red Tree
recommendations.blurb: I’m getting into Spooky Season by discovering Caitlín Kiernan, whose The Red Tree is a really fun combo of nesting narratives and folk horror.

recommendations.name: Ask Brave
recommendations.blurb: Brave Search now has Ask Brave, like AI mode in Google but without the creepy tracking.

recommendations.name: Simply Aviation
recommendations.blurb: My partner and I have been crushing Simply Aviation reviews on YouTube. The channel focuses on economy! You can see differences that will make crossing oceans just a little nicer when you can’t lay flat.

recommendations.name: Rode Wireless Go Gen 3
recommendations.blurb: I just got a Rode Wireless Go Gen 3, and it’s... magical? Local recordings, solid wireless sync, great battery life. But it comes with the goofiest USB-C charger that is sort of adorable.

recommendations.name: Ugmonk’s Analog
recommendations.blurb: A couple months ago, I moved all of my day-to-day task management out of apps and into Ugmonk’s Analog paper and pencil system. It’s been great. De-digitizing key parts of my day is more thoughtful, less distracting, and just more fun than trying to manage the nth productivity app on my phone.

recommendations.name: Hades II
recommendations.blurb: Hades II on the Switch 2, feels just as good to play as the original. Haven’t beaten it yet, but it feels like I’m endlessly unlocking new features and advancing, which makes it disgustingly addictive.

recommendations.name: exclude a single song from your “taste profile,”
recommendations.blurb: There was a lot of news this week, but at least in my life there was nothing more exciting than one tiny new Spotify feature: you can now exclude a single song from your “taste profile,” which means Spotify won’t use it to program recommendations or playlists.
